chunks: And ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn and the group of my scholars narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Umar, from ‘Uyaynah the seller of reeds, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allāh will register him among the highest in ‘Illīyīn.

key_terms.أَعْلَى عِلِّيِّينَ: The highest in ‘Illīyīn (a high rank in paradise)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husain with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the profound spiritual elevation of visiting Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) with 'irfan' (gnostic recognition) of his divine right, linking this act to the celestial record of the 'A’lā ‘Illīyyīn. This tradition underscores the Shia belief that the martyr of Karbala serves as a cosmic axis, where his grave becomes a locus of divine proximity, elevating the visitor to the highest echelons of paradise alongside the prophets and righteous.
